title: Innsbruck Nordkette Cable Railways & Top of Innsbruck
name: Innsbruck Nordkette Cable Railways & Top of Innsbruck
kurzbeschreibung: The Innsbrucker Nordkettenbahnen: from the old town in 20 minutes to over 2,250 m into the high-alpine Karwendel featuring Zaha Hadid stations and the Top of Innsbruck.
beschreibung:
Overview

The spectacular Innsbrucker Nordkettenbahnen connect the historic city center of Tyrol's capital Innsbruck directly with the high-alpine mountain world of the Nordkette in the Naturpark Karwendel. In just around twenty minutes, passengers travel from the modern valley station at the Congress center at 560 meters above sea level up to Hafelekar at 2,269 meters, ascending more than 1,700 vertical meters. The unique symbiosis of forward-looking modern architecture in the heart of the city and rugged limestone peaks makes the Nordkettenbahn one of Tyrol's most famous landmarks.

Architecture & High Mountain Experience

The journey begins with the futuristic Hungerburgbahn, whose sweeping, snow-white glass and shell stations were designed by world-renowned star architect Zaha Hadid and mimic natural glacier ice formations. After crossing the Inn river, the track leads across a striking cable-stayed bridge and through several tunnels up to Hungerburg. From there, visitors glide aboard the two panoramic cable car sections of the Nordkettenbahn via Seegrube (1,905 m) directly up to the top station at Hafelekar. Arriving at the summit reveals the breathtaking panorama of the Top of Innsbruck: on one side lies the Alpine city of Innsbruck with the silvery ribbon of the Inn river at your feet, while on the other side you gaze into the untouched, dramatic wilderness of the Karwendel. In summer, the area serves as the starting point for scenic hikes such as the Goetheweg; in winter, the Hafelekarrinne tempts freeriders as one of the steepest ski routes in Europe.

Visit & Getting There

The Nordkettenbahnen operate daily year-round (Hungerburgbahn from 08:00, cable cars from 08:30 to 17:00; brief maintenance closures in spring and late autumn). Ticket prices (as of the 2025/2026 season): Top of Innsbruck ticket (complete round trip) adults approx. €47.00, seniors approx. €42.00, youth (16–18 years) approx. €37.50, children (6–15 years) approx. €23.50. Holders of the Innsbruck Card enjoy free travel! Getting there: The Congress valley station is centrally located in Innsbruck's historic old town on Rennweg and is easily reachable in just a few minutes from the Zentrum/Congress parking garages or by public bus (lines TS, 4, M).

Tips

The cable cars, stations, and viewing terraces at Seegrube are barrier-free and wheelchair accessible; the short walk from the Hafelekar mountain station to the summit cross (approx. 10–15 minutes on foot) follows a well-maintained gravel path and requires sturdy footwear. Stop by the Alpenlounge Seegrube restaurant and savor traditional Tyrolean specialties with unique city views from the panorama terrace.
